stem: A 42-year-old with congenital ectodermal dysplasia has oligodontia, reduced salivary secretion, thin alveolar ridges and several short clinical crowns. A clinician proposes the same bridge design used for a patient with normally developed supporting tissues.
lead: Which feature most changes the prosthodontic plan?

options.A: Ignore xerostomia because it affects only removable dentures
options.B: Coordinate management of residual dentition, salivary risk, ridge anatomy and long-term prosthesis adaptability.
options.C: Prepare every residual tooth for full coverage regardless of crown length
options.D: Use ridge radiographic height as the only criterion
options.E: Fabricate immediate definitive fixed implant restorations without growth assessment

solution:
PROPOSED BEST ANSWER: B - Coordinate management of residual dentition, salivary risk, ridge anatomy and long-term prosthesis adaptability.

CLINICAL REASONING: Congenital developmental differences affect abutment prognosis, caries risk, support, growth and future maintenance; a standard bridge template is inadequate.

WHY EACH ALTERNATIVE IS LESS APPROPRIATE:
A. Ignore xerostomia because it affects only removable dentures - Low saliva increases caries, mucosal and prosthetic complications.
C. Prepare every residual tooth for full coverage regardless of crown length - This sacrifices scarce abutment tissue without demonstrating benefit.
D. Use ridge radiographic height as the only criterion - Ridge volume does not account for salivary, mucosal, tooth or functional limitations.
E. Fabricate immediate definitive fixed implant restorations without growth assessment - Growth status and anatomy may preclude such placement.

stem: In a patient assessed for a cracked molar, a cold test is negative after extensive calcification; percussion is mildly positive, and an intraoral radiograph has no definite apical lesion. The patient has prolonged intermittent pain.
lead: How should the negative cold test be interpreted?

options.A: Treat it as one imperfect diagnostic observation and integrate repeated testing, control teeth, clinical symptoms, probing and imaging.
options.B: Diagnose pulp necrosis with certainty from the cold test alone
options.C: Assume a normal radiograph excludes apical disease
options.D: Proceed directly to extraction without confirming restorability
options.E: Prescribe antibiotics as a diagnostic trial

solution:
PROPOSED BEST ANSWER: A - Treat it as one imperfect diagnostic observation and integrate repeated testing, control teeth, clinical symptoms, probing and imaging.

CLINICAL REASONING: Sensibility tests assess neural response rather than directly measuring pulp blood flow and may be falsely negative.

D. Proceed directly to extraction without confirming restorability - A differential and prognosis are still required.
E. Prescribe antibiotics as a diagnostic trial - Antibiotics do not clarify pulpal vitality and are not routine pain management.
